thread.title: Analyst Downgrades Chipmaker Super Micro Following Chinese Hacking Report

title: Analyst Downgrades Chipmaker Super Micro Following Chinese Hacking Report
text:
Text size Piero Cruciatti/AFP/Getty Images
Maxim Group analyst Nehal Chokshi ended his bullish call on the chip maker at the center of Bloomberg’s investigation into Chinese hacking of servers, but not as decisively as one might expect.
Bloomberg on Thursday reported that Amazon.com (AMZN) and Apple (AAPL) found malicious chips on motherboards purchased by Super Micro Computer (SMCI), which all three companies vigorously denied . On Friday, Chokshi downgraded Super Micro’s stock to “hold” from “buy.”
He also removed his previous price target of $50. The shares were recently trading at $12.43 after a 40% plunge Thursday and a roughly 1% drop in Friday’s session.
Chokshi tends to side with Apple’s denial of the report amid “no verifiable facts” in the story, he wrote Friday. Apple, in a statement posted online , contends that the outlet was “confusing their story with a previously-reported 2016 incident in which we discovered an infected driver on a single Super Micro server in one of our labs.”
The company also said that the incident in question wasn’t deemed to be a “targeted attack against Apple.”
Chokshi said he also supports Super Micro’s position that if China were able to pull off this sort of attack on motherboards, it would be an industrywide issue, not just one specific to Super Micro.
That said, “given the level of detail” in the Bloomberg report, Chokshi wrote that he was “uncomfortable fully dismissing the risk as not being [Super Micro] specific.”
Apple, Amazon, and Super Micro didn’t immediately respond to Barron’s request for additional comment on the Bloomberg story beyond their statements posted online.
